author: nzfauna
coverageDescription:
Selected bones from within the skeleton of a dog (*Canis lupus familiaris*).

The 3D Dog Bone Project is a collaboration between the Institute of Vet, Animal & Biomedical Sciences and the Institute of Natural and Mathematical Sciences at Massey University, New Zealand.

Click on the annotated bones to access downloadable models. Individual bones are high-fidelity 3D scans that are suitable for use as anatomically-accurate teaching resources. 

The 3D silhouette is 'Low poly doggy', kindly provided by Joe McDowall. Check out the original at https://sketchfab.com/models/1c8c763518ab4751bfcddf0b6a34011a
reason: Selección parcial y silueta low-poly, no esqueleto íntegro. Atribución y SA; auditar licencia individual de cada hueso.

author: nzfauna
coverageDescription:
Digital replica of the upper skull from a dog (*Canis lupus familiaris*). 

The 3D Dog Bone Project is a collaboration between the Institute of Vet, Animal & Biomedical Sciences and the Institute of Natural and Mathematical Sciences at Massey University, New Zealand.
This model is a high-fidelity 3D scan and is suitable for use as an anatomically-accurate teaching resource. Note though that the anatomical detail within the nose and foramen magnum is not well-resolved. 3D scan data were collected using an SLS-2 structured light scanner (DAVID Vision Systems) and data were processed to create a model with 0.3 mm resolution. This model can be downloaded and 3D printed.

Information about the size of the scanned bone is coming soon.

For placement of this bone in the dog skeleton see: https://sketchfab.com/models/65a6c5db1c4c477aba475af5d86d59a5
reason: Craneo superior aislado; autor advierte resolución incompleta nasal/foramen magnum. SA obligatorio.

author: nzfauna
coverageDescription:
Digital replica of the atlas from a dog (*Canis lupus familiaris*). The atlas is the vertebra in the neck that sits just behind the head and is also identified as C1, the first cervical vertebra.

The 3D Dog Bone Project is a collaboration between the Institute of Vet, Animal & Biomedical Sciences and the Institute of Natural and Mathematical Sciences at Massey University, New Zealand.
This model is a high-fidelity 3D scan and is suitable for use as an anatomically-accurate teaching resource. 3D scan data were collected using an SLS-2 structured light scanner (DAVID Vision Systems) and data were processed to create a model with 0.2 mm resolution. This model can be downloaded and 3D printed.

Information about the size of the scanned bone is coming soon.

For placement of this bone in the dog skeleton see: https://sketchfab.com/models/65a6c5db1c4c477aba475af5d86d59a5
reason: Atlas aislado; NC obligatorio. No heredar BY-SA del ensamblaje parcial.
